// diagnostic E0434

Jet.FailureMarkRequired

A call or loop header that can pass a typed failure up to its caller is written without `?` or `?(text)`.

What

A call or loop header that can pass a typed failure up to its caller is written without `?` or `?(text)`.

Why

Every early exit from a typed `E!` failure is visible in source text so readers see where the function can stop early.

Fix

Write `?` after the call (or `call()?.member` to chain, `loop? x in source` for failing iterators, or `?(text)` to add a context frame). `jet fmt` writes every mark automatically.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.FailureMarkRequired: Tests/UI/failures_explicit_policy.stderr.

Error: Jet.FailureMarkRequired: `parse` can fail, so the call is written with `?`
  --> Tests/UI/failures_explicit_policy.jet:11:11
    |
 11 |     rows: parse(path)
    |           ^^^^^
 Why: Every call that can pass a failure up writes `?` so each early exit shows in the text
 Fix: Write `?` after the call, or `?(text)` to add a context frame
